description: Comprehensive question bank derived from FDA & SDA Computer Knowledge 18.5 MS Office notes. Questions cover all concepts, features, shortcuts, functions, formats, and exam-relevant points from the source material. All questions are uniquely framed to avoid duplication.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Microsoft Office?

options.A: A single word processing application
options.B: A family of productivity applications developed by Microsoft
options.C: An operating system developed by Microsoft
options.D: A web browser developed by Microsoft

questions.explanation: Microsoft Office is a family of productivity applications developed by Microsoft for tasks such as word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, email and collaboration.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a commonly included application in Microsoft Office?

options.A: Microsoft Word
options.B: Microsoft Excel
options.C: Adobe Photoshop
options.D: Microsoft PowerPoint

questions.explanation: Common Office applications include Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and may include Outlook, Access, OneNote and Publisher. Adobe Photoshop is not part of Microsoft Office.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a productivity application?

options.A: Software designed to help users complete work such as preparing documents and analysing data
options.B: Software used only for playing games
options.C: Software used only for browsing the internet
options.D: Software used only for editing videos

questions.explanation: A productivity application is software designed to help users complete work such as preparing documents, analysing data, creating presentations, communicating and organising information.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the key difference between Microsoft Office and Microsoft 365?

options.A: Microsoft Office is free while Microsoft 365 is paid
options.B: Microsoft Office is a one-time-purchase edition while Microsoft 365 is a subscription service
options.C: Microsoft Office is only for Windows while Microsoft 365 is only for Mac
options.D: Microsoft Office is cloud-based while Microsoft 365 is desktop-based

questions.explanation: Microsoft Office commonly refers to the productivity application suite or a one-time-purchase edition, while Microsoft 365 is a subscription service that provides Office applications and may include cloud storage, collaboration and other services.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Ribbon in Microsoft Office applications?

options.A: A toolbar at the bottom of the window
options.B: A command interface at the top that organises tools into tabs and groups
options.C: A type of document template
options.D: A file format used by Office applications

questions.explanation: The Ribbon is the command interface at the top of many Office applications. It organises tools into tabs and groups, such as Home, Insert, Layout, Review and View.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Quick Access Toolbar?

options.A: A toolbar that provides quick access to frequently used commands such as Save, Undo and Redo
options.B: A toolbar that only contains formatting options
options.C: A toolbar that is only available in Excel
options.D: A toolbar that is used to insert images

questions.explanation: The Quick Access Toolbar is a customisable toolbar that provides quick access to frequently used commands, commonly including Save, Undo and Redo.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a template in an Office application?

options.A: A pre-designed file containing layouts, styles, formatting or content placeholders that users can reuse
options.B: A type of macro
options.C: A file format used for saving documents
options.D: A keyboard shortcut

questions.explanation: A template is a pre-designed file containing layouts, styles, formatting or content placeholders that users can reuse to create consistent documents, workbooks or presentations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the default file format of modern Microsoft Word documents?

options.A: .doc
options.B: .docx
options.C: .docm
options.D: .txt

questions.explanation: Modern Office applications commonly use Office Open XML formats. Word uses .docx by default.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the default file format of modern Microsoft Excel workbooks?

options.A: .xls
options.B: .xlsx
options.C: .xlsm
options.D: .csv

questions.explanation: Modern Excel workbooks commonly use the .xlsx extension by default.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the default file format of modern Microsoft PowerPoint presentations?

options.A: .ppt
options.B: .pptx
options.C: .pptm
options.D: .pps

questions.explanation: Modern PowerPoint presentations commonly use the .pptx extension by default.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which file extension is used for a macro-enabled Word document?

options.A: .docx
options.B: .docm
options.C: .doc
options.D: .dotx

questions.explanation: A macro-enabled Word document commonly uses the .docm extension.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which file extension is used for a macro-enabled Excel workbook?

options.A: .xlsx
options.B: .xlsm
options.C: .xls
options.D: .xltx

questions.explanation: A macro-enabled Excel workbook commonly uses the .xlsm extension.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which file extension is used for a macro-enabled PowerPoint presentation?

options.A: .pptx
options.B: .pptm
options.C: .ppt
options.D: .potx

questions.explanation: A macro-enabled PowerPoint presentation commonly uses the .pptm extension.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Save command?

options.A: To store changes to the current file
options.B: To close the application
options.C: To print the document
options.D: To open a new file

questions.explanation: The Save command stores changes to the current file. If the file has not previously been saved, the application may ask the user to choose a file name and location.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of Save As?

options.A: To save a document or create a copy under a different name, location or file format
options.B: To delete the current document
options.C: To print the document
options.D: To undo the last action

questions.explanation: Save As saves a document or creates a copy under a different name, location or file format, depending on the application.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is AutoSave in Microsoft 365?

options.A: A feature that automatically saves changes to supported files stored in supported cloud locations
options.B: A feature that automatically closes the application
options.C: A feature that automatically prints documents
options.D: A feature that automatically deletes files

questions.explanation: AutoSave automatically saves changes to supported files stored in supported cloud locations, such as OneDrive or SharePoint.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is AutoRecover in Microsoft Office?

options.A: A feature that periodically saves recovery information so unsaved work may be recovered after a crash
options.B: A feature that automatically saves files to the cloud
options.C: A feature that automatically backs up files to an external drive
options.D: A feature that automatically restores deleted files

questions.explanation: AutoRecover periodically saves recovery information for supported Office applications so that unsaved work may be recovered after a crash or unexpected closure. It is not a substitute for saving regularly.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Clipboard in Office applications?

options.A: A temporary storage area for copied or cut content
options.B: A permanent storage area for all documents
options.C: A type of file format
options.D: A keyboard shortcut

questions.explanation: The Clipboard temporarily holds copied or cut content, such as text, cells, pictures and objects, so that it can be pasted elsewhere.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Undo do in Office applications?

options.A: Reverses a recent supported action
options.B: Reapplies an action that was undone
options.C: Deletes the entire document
options.D: Saves the document

questions.explanation: Undo reverses a recent supported action, while Redo reapplies an action that was undone.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Redo do in Office applications?

options.A: Reverses a recent supported action
options.B: Reapplies an action that was undone
options.C: Deletes the entire document
options.D: Saves the document

questions.explanation: Redo reapplies an action that was undone.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the status bar in Office applications?

options.A: An information area at the bottom of the application window that displays context-specific information
options.B: A toolbar at the top of the window
options.C: A type of document template
options.D: A keyboard shortcut

questions.explanation: The status bar is an information area, usually at the bottom of the application window, that displays context-specific information such as page number, word count, selection statistics, view controls or zoom.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of Print Preview?

options.A: To display how a document, worksheet or presentation is expected to appear when printed
options.B: To print the document immediately
options.C: To save the document as a PDF
options.D: To edit the document

questions.explanation: Print Preview displays how a document, worksheet or presentation is expected to appear when printed, allowing the user to check layout and page arrangement before printing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Microsoft Word?

options.A: A spreadsheet application
options.B: A word-processing application used to create, edit, format, save, review and print text-based documents
options.C: A presentation application
options.D: An email application

questions.explanation: Microsoft Word is a word-processing application used to create, edit, format, save, review and print text-based documents.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is word processing?

options.A: The use of software to create, edit, format, store and print text documents
options.B: The use of software to create spreadsheets
options.C: The use of software to create presentations
options.D: The use of software to edit images

questions.explanation: Word processing is the use of software to create, edit, format, store and print text documents.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the default file extension of a modern Word document?

options.A: .doc
options.B: .docx
options.C: .docm
options.D: .txt

questions.explanation: The default modern Word document extension is .docx.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the extension of a macro-enabled Word document?

options.A: .docx
options.B: .docm
options.C: .doc
options.D: .dotx

questions.explanation: A macro-enabled Word document commonly uses the .docm extension.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the older Microsoft Word document extension?

options.A: .docx
options.B: .docm
options.C: .doc
options.D: .rtf

questions.explanation: The older binary Word document format commonly uses the .doc extension.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How can a new blank document be created in Word?

options.A: File > New > Blank document or Ctrl + N
options.B: File > Open
options.C: File > Save
options.D: File > Print

questions.explanation: A user can select File > New > Blank document, or use the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + N in the desktop application.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the cursor or insertion point in Word?

options.A: The blinking vertical marker that indicates where newly typed text will appear
options.B: A type of font
options.C: A page break
options.D: A header

questions.explanation: The insertion point is the blinking vertical marker that indicates where newly typed text will appear in the document.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is text selection in Word?

options.A: Highlighting text so that an operation such as formatting, copying, cutting or deleting can be applied
options.B: Changing the font colour of text
options.C: Inserting a table
options.D: Creating a new document

questions.explanation: Text selection highlights a character, word, sentence, paragraph or larger section so that an operation such as formatting, copying, cutting or deleting can be applied.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between Save and Save As in Word?

options.A: Save updates the current file, while Save As creates a new file or saves under a different name, location or format
options.B: Save creates a new file, while Save As updates the current file
options.C: Save and Save As are identical
options.D: Save closes the file, while Save As prints it

questions.explanation: Save updates the current file, while Save As creates a new file or saves the document under a different name, location or format.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a word count in Word?

options.A: A feature that reports the number of words and may also display characters, paragraphs and pages
options.B: A feature that counts the number of tables in a document
options.C: A feature that counts the number of images in a document
options.D: A feature that counts the number of pages only

questions.explanation: Word count reports the number of words and may also display characters, paragraphs and pages, depending on the version and selected options.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Navigation Pane in Word?

options.A: A pane that helps users search document text and navigate through headings or pages
options.B: A pane that displays the document's word count
options.C: A pane that displays the document's file properties
options.D: A pane that displays the document's print preview

questions.explanation: The Navigation Pane helps users search document text and navigate through headings or pages in supported versions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of the spelling and grammar checker in Word?

options.A: It identifies possible spelling, grammar and writing issues and may suggest corrections
options.B: It automatically corrects all errors without review
options.C: It translates the document into another language
options.D: It formats the document

questions.explanation: The spelling and grammar checker identifies possible spelling, grammar and writing issues and may suggest corrections; its suggestions should be reviewed because they are not always correct.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is AutoCorrect in Word?

options.A: A feature that automatically replaces certain commonly mistyped words or character combinations with configured replacements
options.B: A feature that automatically saves the document
options.C: A feature that automatically formats the document
options.D: A feature that automatically prints the document

questions.explanation: AutoCorrect automatically replaces certain commonly mistyped words, character combinations or text patterns with configured replacements as the user types.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a page break in Word?

options.A: A feature that forces the following content to begin on a new page
options.B: A feature that divides the document into sections
options.C: A feature that inserts a table
options.D: A feature that inserts a header

questions.explanation: A page break forces the following content to begin on a new page without requiring repeated blank lines.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a section break in Word?

options.A: A break that divides a document into sections so that different parts can have different page layouts, headers, footers, columns or numbering settings
options.B: A break that forces content to begin on a new page
options.C: A break that inserts a blank line
options.D: A break that inserts a table

questions.explanation: A section break divides a document into sections so that different parts can have different page layouts, headers, footers, columns or numbering settings.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between a page break and a section break?

options.A: A page break starts content on a new page; a section break creates a new document section and can allow different layout or formatting settings
options.B: A page break creates a new section; a section break starts content on a new page
options.C: They are identical
options.D: A page break is used only in Excel; a section break is used only in Word

questions.explanation: A page break starts content on a new page; a section break creates a new document section and can allow different layout or formatting settings in that section.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is text formatting in Word?

options.A: Changing the appearance of characters such as font, font size, colour, bold, italic, underline, highlighting and character spacing
options.B: Changing the page margins
options.C: Inserting a table
options.D: Creating a new document

questions.explanation: Text formatting changes the appearance of characters, such as font, font size, colour, bold, italic, underline, highlighting and character spacing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is paragraph formatting in Word?

options.A: Controlling the layout of paragraphs including alignment, indentation, line spacing, spacing before or after paragraphs, borders and bullets or numbering
options.B: Changing the font colour
options.C: Inserting a header
options.D: Creating a table of contents

questions.explanation: Paragraph formatting controls the layout of paragraphs, including alignment, indentation, line spacing, spacing before or after paragraphs, borders and bullets or numbering.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a font?

options.A: A typeface design used to display text, such as Arial, Calibri, Times New Roman or Aptos
options.B: The size of characters
options.C: The colour of text
options.D: The alignment of text

questions.explanation: A font is a typeface design used to display text, such as Arial, Calibri, Times New Roman or Aptos.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is font size measured in?

options.A: Points (pt)
options.B: Pixels
options.C: Centimetres
options.D: Inches

questions.explanation: Font size specifies the size of characters and is commonly measured in points (pt). One point is 1/72 of an inch.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is bold formatting?

options.A: Formatting that makes text appear heavier or darker to emphasise it
options.B: Formatting that slants text
options.C: Formatting that places a line beneath text
options.D: Formatting that applies a background colour behind text

questions.explanation: Bold formatting makes text appear heavier or darker to emphasise it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is italic formatting?

options.A: Formatting that slants text and is commonly used for emphasis, titles or certain editorial conventions
options.B: Formatting that makes text heavier
options.C: Formatting that places a line beneath text
options.D: Formatting that applies a background colour

questions.explanation: Italic formatting slants text and is commonly used for emphasis, titles or certain editorial conventions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is underline formatting?

options.A: Formatting that places a line beneath selected text
options.B: Formatting that slants text
options.C: Formatting that makes text heavier
options.D: Formatting that applies a background colour

questions.explanation: Underline formatting places a line beneath selected text.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is text highlighting?

options.A: Applying a background colour behind selected text to make it stand out
options.B: Making text bold
options.C: Making text italic
options.D: Underlining text

questions.explanation: Text highlighting applies a background colour behind selected text to make it stand out.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is text alignment?

options.A: It determines how text is positioned horizontally within a paragraph or text area
options.B: It determines the font size
options.C: It determines the colour of text
options.D: It determines the line spacing

questions.explanation: Text alignment determines how text is positioned horizontally within a paragraph or text area.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the common paragraph alignment options in Word?

options.A: Align Left, Centre, Align Right and Justify
options.B: Bold, Italic, Underline and Strike
options.C: Portrait, Landscape, A4 and Letter
options.D: Header, Footer, Margin and Indent

questions.explanation: The common options are Align Left, Centre, Align Right and Justify.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does left alignment mean?

options.A: It positions paragraph text evenly along the left margin while the right edge remains uneven
options.B: It positions paragraph text centrally
options.C: It positions paragraph text evenly along the right margin
options.D: It adjusts spacing so text aligns with both margins

questions.explanation: Left alignment positions paragraph text evenly along the left margin while the right edge remains uneven.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does centre alignment mean?

options.A: It positions paragraph text centrally between the left and right margins
options.B: It positions text along the left margin
options.C: It positions text along the right margin
options.D: It adjusts spacing so text aligns with both margins

questions.explanation: Centre alignment positions paragraph text centrally between the left and right margins.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does right alignment mean?

options.A: It positions paragraph text evenly along the right margin while the left edge remains uneven
options.B: It positions text centrally
options.C: It positions text along the left margin
options.D: It adjusts spacing so text aligns with both margins

questions.explanation: Right alignment positions paragraph text evenly along the right margin while the left edge remains uneven.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does justified alignment mean?

options.A: It adjusts spacing between words so that text lines align with both the left and right margins, except commonly the final line of a paragraph
options.B: It positions text only along the left margin
options.C: It positions text only along the right margin
options.D: It centres text between margins

questions.explanation: Justified alignment adjusts spacing between words so that text lines align with both the left and right margins, except commonly the final line of a paragraph.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is line spacing?

options.A: The vertical distance between lines of text within a paragraph
options.B: The space placed before or after a paragraph
options.C: The space between characters
options.D: The space between page margins

questions.explanation: Line spacing is the vertical distance between lines of text within a paragraph.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is paragraph spacing?

options.A: The space placed before or after a paragraph to separate it from surrounding content
options.B: The vertical distance between lines of text
options.C: The space between characters
options.D: The space between page margins

questions.explanation: Paragraph spacing is the space placed before or after a paragraph to separate it from surrounding content.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is indentation in Word?

options.A: It moves a paragraph or selected lines inward from the page margins
options.B: It moves text outward from the page margins
options.C: It changes the font size
options.D: It changes the text colour

questions.explanation: Indentation moves a paragraph or selected lines inward from the page margins. Common types include left, right, first-line and hanging indents.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a first-line indent?

options.A: It moves only the first line of a paragraph inward from the left margin
options.B: It leaves the first line at the margin and moves subsequent lines inward
options.C: It moves all lines inward
options.D: It moves all lines outward

questions.explanation: A first-line indent moves only the first line of a paragraph inward from the left margin.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a hanging indent?

options.A: It leaves the first line at the margin and moves subsequent lines inward
options.B: It moves only the first line inward
options.C: It moves all lines inward
options.D: It moves all lines outward

questions.explanation: A hanging indent leaves the first line at the margin and moves subsequent lines inward; it is commonly used in bibliographies and reference lists.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are bullets in Word?

options.A: Symbols used to present items in an unordered list
options.B: Numbers used to present items in an ordered list
options.C: Lines placed beneath text
options.D: Background colours applied to text

questions.explanation: Bullets are symbols used to present items in an unordered list.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is numbering in Word?

options.A: Assigning ordered numbers or letters to list items to show sequence or hierarchy
options.B: Assigning symbols to list items
options.C: Applying a background colour
options.D: Underlining text

questions.explanation: Numbering assigns ordered numbers or letters to list items to show sequence or hierarchy.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Format Painter in Word?

options.A: A tool that copies formatting from selected text or an object and applies it to another selection without copying the content
options.B: A tool that copies text content
options.C: A tool that inserts a table
options.D: A tool that changes the page layout

questions.explanation: Format Painter copies formatting from selected text or an object and applies it to another selection without copying the original content.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Clear All Formatting in Word?

options.A: It removes direct formatting from selected text and returns it to the formatting defined by the applicable style or default settings
options.B: It deletes all text in the document
options.C: It removes all images from the document
options.D: It clears the Clipboard

questions.explanation: Clear All Formatting removes direct formatting from selected text and returns it to the formatting defined by the applicable style or default settings.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a style in Word?

options.A: A named collection of formatting settings that can be applied consistently to text or paragraphs
options.B: A type of font
options.C: A page layout
options.D: A file format

questions.explanation: A style is a named collection of formatting settings that can be applied consistently to text or paragraphs, such as Normal, Title and Heading 1.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why are heading styles important in Word?

options.A: They create a consistent document structure and support features such as automatic tables of contents, Navigation Pane browsing and accessible document organisation
options.B: They change the font colour only
options.C: They insert images
options.D: They create page breaks

questions.explanation: Heading styles create a consistent document structure and support features such as automatic tables of contents, Navigation Pane browsing and accessible document organisation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a theme in Word?

options.A: A coordinated set of design choices, such as colours, fonts and effects, that helps maintain a consistent appearance
options.B: A type of page break
options.C: A table style
options.D: A file format

questions.explanation: A theme is a coordinated set of design choices, such as colours, fonts and effects, that helps maintain a consistent appearance across a document.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a watermark in Word?

options.A: Text or an image displayed behind document content, often used to mark a document as Draft, Confidential or Sample
options.B: A type of header
options.C: A page border
options.D: A footnote

questions.explanation: A watermark is text or an image displayed behind document content, often used to mark a document as Draft, Confidential or Sample.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is columns formatting in Word?

options.A: It divides text into vertical sections, similar to a newspaper layout
options.B: It divides text into horizontal sections
options.C: It inserts a table
options.D: It changes the font size

questions.explanation: Columns formatting divides text into vertical sections, similar to a newspaper layout.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a drop cap in Word?

options.A: An enlarged initial letter at the beginning of a paragraph, often extending down multiple lines
options.B: A type of bullet
options.C: A page header
options.D: A footnote

questions.explanation: A drop cap is an enlarged initial letter at the beginning of a paragraph, often extending down multiple lines.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Word Tables, Page Setup, Headers and Footers
questions.question: What is a table in Word?

options.A: A structure that organises information into rows and columns, with each intersection forming a cell
options.B: A type of page break
options.C: A header
options.D: A footnote

questions.explanation: A table organises information into rows and columns, with each intersection forming a cell.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Word Tables, Page Setup, Headers and Footers
questions.question: What is a row in a Word table?

options.A: A horizontal arrangement of cells in a table
options.B: A vertical arrangement of cells in a table
options.C: The intersection of a row and column
options.D: A line around a cell

questions.explanation: A row is a horizontal arrangement of cells in a table.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Word Tables, Page Setup, Headers and Footers
questions.question: What is a column in a Word table?

options.A: A vertical arrangement of cells in a table
options.B: A horizontal arrangement of cells in a table
options.C: The intersection of a row and column
options.D: A line around a cell

questions.explanation: A column is a vertical arrangement of cells in a table.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Word Tables, Page Setup, Headers and Footers
questions.question: What is a cell in a Word table?

options.A: The individual box formed at the intersection of a row and a column in a table
options.B: A horizontal arrangement of data
options.C: A vertical arrangement of data
options.D: A line around the table

questions.explanation: A cell is the individual box formed at the intersection of a row and a column in a table.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Word Tables, Page Setup, Headers and Footers
questions.question: How can a table be inserted in Word?

options.A: Through Insert > Table by selecting a grid size or using the available table-insertion options
options.B: Through File > Open
options.C: Through Review > Track Changes
options.D: Through View > Zoom

questions.explanation: A table can be inserted through Insert > Table by selecting a grid size or using the available table-insertion options.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Word Tables, Page Setup, Headers and Footers
questions.question: What does merging cells mean in Word?

options.A: Combining two or more selected adjacent cells into one larger cell
options.B: Dividing one selected cell into multiple rows or columns
options.C: Deleting a cell
options.D: Adding a border to a cell

questions.explanation: Merging cells combines two or more selected adjacent cells into one larger cell.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Word Tables, Page Setup, Headers and Footers
questions.question: What does splitting cells mean in Word?

options.A: Dividing one selected cell into multiple rows or columns
options.B: Combining two or more cells into one
options.C: Deleting a cell
options.D: Adding a border to a cell

questions.explanation: Splitting cells divides one selected cell into multiple rows or columns.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Word Tables, Page Setup, Headers and Footers
questions.question: What is a table border?

options.A: A line applied around or between table cells to define the table's structure
options.B: A background colour applied to cells
options.C: A method of merging cells
options.D: A method of splitting cells

questions.explanation: A table border is a line applied around or between table cells to define the table's structure.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge

options.C: It hides selected rows or columns
options.D: It deletes selected rows or columns

questions.explanation: Freeze Panes keeps selected rows or columns visible while the user scrolls through the rest of a worksheet.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Workbook, Worksheet, Rows, Columns and Cells
questions.question: What is the purpose of merging cells in Excel?

options.A: It combines selected adjacent cells into one larger cell, often for headings; only the content in the upper-left cell is retained in a standard merge operation
options.B: It splits one cell into multiple cells
options.C: It hides selected cells
options.D: It deletes selected cells

questions.explanation: Merging cells combines selected adjacent cells into one larger cell, often for headings. Only the content in the upper-left cell is retained in a standard merge operation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Workbook, Worksheet, Rows, Columns and Cells
questions.question: What is Wrap Text in Excel?

options.A: It displays long cell content on multiple lines within the same cell so that the content can be read without requiring a single long line
options.B: It converts text to uppercase
options.C: It converts text to lowercase
options.D: It removes spaces from text

questions.explanation: Wrap Text displays long cell content on multiple lines within the same cell so that the content can be read without requiring a single long line.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Workbook, Worksheet, Rows, Columns and Cells
questions.question: What is AutoFit in Excel?

options.A: It adjusts row height or column width to fit the contents of the cells, subject to the selected range and settings
options.B: It automatically formats the worksheet with a specific style
options.C: It automatically inserts a new worksheet
options.D: It automatically deletes empty rows

questions.explanation: AutoFit adjusts row height or column width to fit the contents of the cells, subject to the selected range and settings.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What types of data can be entered into an Excel cell?

options.A: Text, numbers, dates, times, logical values, formulas or functions
options.B: Only text and numbers
options.C: Only formulas
options.D: Only dates and times

questions.explanation: A cell can contain text, numbers, dates, times, logical values, formulas or functions, depending on the data and cell format.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is a formula in Excel?

options.A: An expression entered into a cell to calculate a result, normally beginning with an equals sign (=)
options.B: A predefined operation such as SUM or AVERAGE
options.C: A type of chart
options.D: A type of cell format

questions.explanation: A formula is an expression entered into a cell to calculate a result. Excel formulas normally begin with an equals sign (=).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is a function in Excel?

options.A: A predefined formula that performs a particular calculation or operation, such as SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, IF or MAX
options.B: A user-created calculation expression
options.C: A type of chart
options.D: A type of cell format

questions.explanation: A function is a predefined formula that performs a particular calculation or operation, such as SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, IF or MAX.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is the difference between a formula and a function in Excel?

options.A: A formula is any user-created calculation expression, while a function is a predefined operation that can be used within a formula
options.B: A formula is a predefined operation, while a function is a user-created expression
options.C: They are identical
options.D: A formula is used only for text, while a function is used only for numbers

questions.explanation: A formula is any user-created calculation expression, while a function is a predefined operation that can be used within a formula. For example, =A1+A2 is a formula, and =SUM(A1:A2) uses a function.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is the purpose of the equals sign in an Excel formula?

options.A: It indicates that the cell entry is a formula to be calculated rather than ordinary text
options.B: It indicates that the cell entry is text
options.C: It indicates that the cell entry is a date
options.D: It indicates that the cell entry is a comment

questions.explanation: The equals sign (=) indicates that the cell entry is a formula to be calculated rather than ordinary text.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: Which of the following is an arithmetic operator in Excel?
questions.explanation: Common arithmetic operators include + for addition, - for subtraction, * for multiplication, / for division, ^ for exponentiation and % for percentage.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is a cell reference in a formula?

options.A: It identifies the cell or range whose value is used in a formula, such as A1 or B2:B10
options.B: It identifies the font used in a cell
options.C: It identifies the colour of a cell
options.D: It identifies the comment attached to a cell

questions.explanation: A cell reference identifies the cell or range whose value is used in a formula, such as A1 or B2:B10.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is a relative cell reference in Excel?

options.A: A reference that changes automatically when a formula is copied to another cell, such as A1
options.B: A reference that remains fixed when a formula is copied, such as $A$1
options.C: A reference that fixes only the column, such as $A1
options.D: A reference that fixes only the row, such as A$1

questions.explanation: A relative reference changes automatically when a formula is copied to another cell. A1 is an example of a relative reference.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is an absolute cell reference in Excel?

options.A: A reference that remains fixed when a formula is copied, using dollar signs before both the column and row, such as $A$1
options.B: A reference that changes automatically when a formula is copied, such as A1
options.C: A reference that fixes only the column, such as $A1
options.D: A reference that fixes only the row, such as A$1

questions.explanation: An absolute reference remains fixed when a formula is copied. It uses dollar signs before both the column and row, such as $A$1.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is a mixed cell reference in Excel?

options.A: A reference that fixes either the column or the row while allowing the other part to change, such as $A1 or A$1
options.B: A reference that changes both column and row when copied
options.C: A reference that fixes both column and row when copied
options.D: A reference that refers to an entire worksheet

questions.explanation: A mixed reference fixes either the column or the row while allowing the other part to change, such as $A1 or A$1.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What does the dollar sign mean in an Excel cell reference?

options.A: It locks the column, row or both in a cell reference when a formula is copied or filled
options.B: It indicates a currency value
options.C: It indicates a percentage value
options.D: It indicates a text value

questions.explanation: The dollar sign locks the column, row or both in a cell reference when a formula is copied or filled.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is the Fill Handle in Excel?

options.A: The small square at the lower-right corner of a selected cell or range that can copy formulas or extend data series when dragged
options.B: A toolbar button that fills cells with colour
options.C: A function that fills empty cells with zeros
options.D: A dialog box used to format cells

questions.explanation: The Fill Handle is the small square at the lower-right corner of a selected cell or range. It can copy formulas or extend data series when dragged.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is AutoFill in Excel?

options.A: It automatically fills adjacent cells with copied content, formulas or recognised series such as dates and numbers
options.B: It automatically formats cells with a specific style
options.C: It automatically deletes empty cells
options.D: It automatically creates charts

questions.explanation: AutoFill automatically fills adjacent cells with copied content, formulas or recognised series such as dates and numbers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is the purpose of Number Format in Excel?

options.A: It controls how values are displayed, such as General, Number, Currency, Accounting, Date, Time, Percentage, Fraction or Scientific, without necessarily changing the underlying numeric value
options.B: It changes the underlying numeric value of a cell
options.C: It changes the formula in a cell
options.D: It changes the font of a cell

questions.explanation: Number Format controls how values are displayed, such as General, Number, Currency, Accounting, Date, Time, Percentage, Fraction or Scientific, without necessarily changing the underlying numeric value.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is percentage formatting in Excel?

options.A: It displays a numeric value as a percentage by multiplying its displayed value by 100 and adding the percent sign
options.B: It displays a numeric value as a currency
options.C: It displays a numeric value as a date
options.D: It displays a numeric value as a fraction

questions.explanation: Percentage formatting displays a numeric value as a percentage by multiplying its displayed value by 100 and adding the percent sign. For example, 0.25 is displayed as 25%.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is currency formatting in Excel?

options.A: It displays numeric values with a currency symbol and specified decimal places
options.B: It displays numeric values as percentages
options.C: It displays numeric values as dates
options.D: It displays numeric values as text

questions.explanation: Currency formatting displays numeric values with a currency symbol and specified decimal places.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is conditional formatting in Excel?

options.A: It automatically changes the appearance of cells when specified rules or conditions are met, helping users identify patterns, values and exceptions
options.B: It automatically changes the formula in a cell
options.C: It automatically changes the worksheet name
options.D: It automatically creates a chart

questions.explanation: Conditional Formatting automatically changes the appearance of cells when specified rules or conditions are met, helping users identify patterns, values and exceptions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is data validation in Excel?

options.A: It controls what users can enter into selected cells, such as whole numbers within a range, dates, text length or values from a drop-down list
options.B: It validates formulas for errors
options.C: It validates charts for accuracy
options.D: It validates the file format

questions.explanation: Data Validation controls what users can enter into selected cells, such as whole numbers within a range, dates, text length or values from a drop-down list.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is a drop-down list in Excel?

options.A: A cell input control commonly created using Data Validation, allowing users to select from predefined values
options.B: A list of recently opened files
options.C: A list of formulas available in Excel
options.D: A list of charts available in Excel

questions.explanation: A drop-down list is a cell input control commonly created using Data Validation, allowing users to select from predefined values.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is a named range in Excel?

options.A: A cell or range of cells assigned a meaningful name, which can make formulas easier to read and maintain
options.B: A range of cells that has been formatted with a specific style
options.C: A range of cells that has been hidden
options.D: A range of cells that has been merged

questions.explanation: A named range is a cell or range of cells assigned a meaningful name, which can make formulas easier to read and maintain.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What is an error value in Excel?

options.A: A value that indicates Excel cannot calculate or interpret a formula as intended
options.B: A value that indicates the formula is correct
options.C: A value that indicates the cell is empty
options.D: A value that indicates the cell is formatted as text

questions.explanation: An error value indicates that Excel cannot calculate or interpret a formula as intended. Common errors include #DIV/0!, #N/A, #NAME?, #REF!, #VALUE! and #NUM!.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What does the #DIV/0! error indicate in Excel?

options.A: A formula attempts to divide a number by zero or by an empty cell treated as zero in the calculation
options.B: A lookup formula cannot find a matching result
options.C: A formula has an invalid cell reference
options.D: A formula has received an argument or data type that is not valid

questions.explanation: #DIV/0! indicates that a formula attempts to divide a number by zero or by an empty cell treated as zero in the calculation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What does the #REF! error mean in Excel?

options.A: It indicates an invalid cell reference, often caused by deleting cells or ranges used by a formula
options.B: It indicates a formula attempts to divide by zero
options.C: It indicates a lookup formula cannot find a matching result
options.D: It indicates a formula has received an invalid data type

questions.explanation: #REF! indicates an invalid cell reference, often caused by deleting cells or ranges used by a formula.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.chapter: Excel Data Entry, Formatting and Formulas
questions.question: What does the #VALUE! error mean in Excel?

options.A: It commonly indicates that a formula has received an argument or data type that is not valid for the operation
options.B: It indicates a formula attempts to divide by zero
options.C: It indicates a lookup formula cannot find a matching result
options.D: It indicates an invalid cell reference

questions.explanation: #VALUE! commonly indicates that a formula has received an argument or data type that is not valid for the operation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the SUM function do in Excel?

options.A: It adds numbers or values in specified cells or ranges
options.B: It calculates the arithmetic mean
options.C: It counts cells containing numbers
options.D: It returns the largest value

questions.explanation: SUM adds numbers or values in specified cells or ranges. Example: =SUM(A1:A10) adds the values from A1 through A10.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the AVERAGE function do in Excel?

options.A: It calculates the arithmetic mean of numeric values
options.B: It adds numbers in a range
options.C: It counts cells containing numbers
options.D: It returns the largest value

questions.explanation: AVERAGE calculates the arithmetic mean of numeric values. Example: =AVERAGE(B1:B10).

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the COUNT function do in Excel?

options.A: It counts cells containing numeric values in the specified arguments or ranges
options.B: It counts non-empty cells
options.C: It counts empty cells
options.D: It adds numbers in a range

questions.explanation: COUNT counts cells containing numeric values in the specified arguments or ranges.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the COUNTA function do in Excel?

options.A: It counts non-empty cells, including cells containing text, numbers, logical values or errors
options.B: It counts only cells containing numbers
options.C: It counts only empty cells
options.D: It adds numbers in a range

questions.explanation: COUNTA counts non-empty cells, including cells containing text, numbers, logical values or errors.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the COUNTBLANK function do in Excel?

options.A: It counts empty cells in a specified range
options.B: It counts non-empty cells
options.C: It counts only cells containing numbers
options.D: It adds numbers in a range

questions.explanation: COUNTBLANK counts empty cells in a specified range.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the MAX function do in Excel?

options.A: It returns the largest numeric value in a set of values or range
options.B: It returns the smallest numeric value
options.C: It calculates the average
options.D: It adds numbers in a range

questions.explanation: MAX returns the largest numeric value in a set of values or range.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the MIN function do in Excel?

options.A: It returns the smallest numeric value in a set of values or range
options.B: It returns the largest numeric value
options.C: It calculates the average
options.D: It adds numbers in a range

questions.explanation: MIN returns the smallest numeric value in a set of values or range.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the PRODUCT function do in Excel?

options.A: It multiplies the numbers supplied as arguments or in specified ranges
options.B: It adds the numbers supplied as arguments
options.C: It calculates the average of numbers
options.D: It counts the numbers supplied as arguments

questions.explanation: PRODUCT multiplies the numbers supplied as arguments or in specified ranges.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the ROUND function do in Excel?

options.A: It rounds a number to a specified number of digits
options.B: It rounds a number up away from zero
options.C: It rounds a number down toward zero
options.D: It returns the absolute value of a number

questions.explanation: ROUND rounds a number to a specified number of digits. Example: =ROUND(12.345,2) returns 12.35.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the IF function do in Excel?

options.A: It tests a logical condition and returns one value when the condition is true and another when it is false
options.B: It adds numbers in a range
options.C: It counts cells in a range
options.D: It returns the largest value in a range

questions.explanation: IF tests a logical condition and returns one value when the condition is true and another when it is false. Example: =IF(A1>=35,"Pass","Fail").

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the AND function do in Excel?

options.A: It returns TRUE if all supplied logical conditions are TRUE; otherwise it returns FALSE
options.B: It returns TRUE if at least one supplied logical condition is TRUE
options.C: It reverses a logical value
options.D: It adds numbers in a range

questions.explanation: AND returns TRUE if all supplied logical conditions are TRUE; otherwise it returns FALSE.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the OR function do in Excel?

options.A: It returns TRUE if at least one supplied logical condition is TRUE; otherwise it returns FALSE
options.B: It returns TRUE only if all supplied logical conditions are TRUE
options.C: It reverses a logical value
options.D: It adds numbers in a range

questions.explanation: OR returns TRUE if at least one supplied logical condition is TRUE; otherwise it returns FALSE.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the NOT function do in Excel?

options.A: It reverses a logical value: TRUE becomes FALSE and FALSE becomes TRUE
options.B: It returns TRUE if all conditions are TRUE
options.C: It returns TRUE if at least one condition is TRUE
options.D: It adds numbers in a range

questions.explanation: NOT reverses a logical value: TRUE becomes FALSE and FALSE becomes TRUE.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the SUMIF function do in Excel?

options.A: It adds values that meet one specified condition
options.B: It counts cells that meet one specified condition
options.C: It calculates the average of cells that meet a specified condition
options.D: It returns the largest value that meets a condition

questions.explanation: SUMIF adds values that meet one specified condition. Example: =SUMIF(A2:A10,"North",B2:B10) adds corresponding values in B2:B10 where A2:A10 equals North.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the COUNTIF function do in Excel?

options.A: It counts cells in a range that meet one specified condition
options.B: It adds values that meet one specified condition
options.C: It calculates the average of cells that meet a specified condition
options.D: It returns the largest value that meets a condition

questions.explanation: COUNTIF counts cells in a range that meet one specified condition. Example: =COUNTIF(C2:C20,">=50").

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the AVERAGEIF function do in Excel?

options.A: It calculates the average of cells that meet a specified condition
options.B: It adds values that meet one specified condition
options.C: It counts cells that meet one specified condition
options.D: It returns the largest value that meets a condition

questions.explanation: AVERAGEIF calculates the average of cells that meet a specified condition.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the VLOOKUP function do in Excel?

options.A: It searches for a value in the first column of a table or range and returns a value from a specified column in the same row
options.B: It searches for a value in the first row of a table and returns a value from a specified row
options.C: It searches a range or array and returns a corresponding value from another range or array
options.D: It joins text from multiple cells

questions.explanation: VLOOKUP searches for a value in the first column of a table or range and returns a value from a specified column in the same row. Its traditional exact-match form uses FALSE as the final argument.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the HLOOKUP function do in Excel?

options.A: It searches for a value in the first row of a table and returns a value from a specified row in the same column
options.B: It searches for a value in the first column of a table and returns a value from a specified column
options.C: It searches a range or array and returns a corresponding value from another range
options.D: It joins text from multiple cells

questions.explanation: HLOOKUP searches for a value in the first row of a table and returns a value from a specified row in the same column.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the XLOOKUP function do in modern Excel?

options.A: It searches a range or array and returns a corresponding value from another range or array, supporting exact matching by default
options.B: It searches for a value in the first column of a table only
options.C: It searches for a value in the first row of a table only
options.D: It joins text from multiple cells

questions.explanation: XLOOKUP searches a range or array and returns a corresponding value from another range or array. It supports exact matching by default and offers more flexible lookup behaviour than traditional VLOOKUP.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the CONCAT function do in Excel?

options.A: It joins text from multiple cells or text strings into one text string
options.B: It splits text into multiple cells
options.C: It converts text to uppercase
options.D: It counts characters in a text string

questions.explanation: CONCAT joins text from multiple cells or text strings into one text string.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the TEXTJOIN function do in Excel?

options.A: It combines text from multiple items or ranges using a specified delimiter and can optionally ignore empty cells
options.B: It splits text into multiple cells
options.C: It converts text to lowercase
options.D: It counts characters in a text string

questions.explanation: TEXTJOIN combines text from multiple items or ranges using a specified delimiter and can optionally ignore empty cells.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the LEFT function do in Excel?

options.A: It returns a specified number of characters from the beginning of a text string
options.B: It returns a specified number of characters from the end of a text string
options.C: It returns a specified number of characters from the middle of a text string
options.D: It returns the number of characters in a text string

questions.explanation: LEFT returns a specified number of characters from the beginning of a text string.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the RIGHT function do in Excel?

options.A: It returns a specified number of characters from the end of a text string
options.B: It returns a specified number of characters from the beginning of a text string
options.C: It returns a specified number of characters from the middle of a text string
options.D: It returns the number of characters in a text string

questions.explanation: RIGHT returns a specified number of characters from the end of a text string.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the MID function do in Excel?

options.A: It returns a specified number of characters from a text string, starting at a given position
options.B: It returns characters from the beginning of a text string
options.C: It returns characters from the end of a text string
options.D: It returns the number of characters in a text string

questions.explanation: MID returns a specified number of characters from a text string, starting at a given position.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the LEN function do in Excel?

options.A: It returns the number of characters in a text string, including spaces
options.B: It returns the first character of a text string
options.C: It returns the last character of a text string
options.D: It converts text to uppercase

questions.explanation: LEN returns the number of characters in a text string, including spaces.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the TRIM function do in Excel?

options.A: It removes leading and trailing spaces and reduces repeated ordinary spaces between words to single spaces
options.B: It removes all spaces from a text string
options.C: It converts text to uppercase
options.D: It converts text to lowercase

questions.explanation: TRIM removes leading and trailing spaces and reduces repeated ordinary spaces between words to single spaces, subject to its handling of the standard space character.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the UPPER function do in Excel?

options.A: It converts text to uppercase letters
options.B: It converts text to lowercase letters
options.C: It capitalises the first letter of each word
options.D: It removes spaces from text

questions.explanation: UPPER converts text to uppercase letters.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the LOWER function do in Excel?

options.A: It converts text to lowercase letters
options.B: It converts text to uppercase letters
options.C: It capitalises the first letter of each word
options.D: It removes spaces from text

questions.explanation: LOWER converts text to lowercase letters.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the PROPER function do in Excel?

options.A: It capitalises the first letter of each word in a text string and converts other letters to lowercase
options.B: It converts all text to uppercase
options.C: It converts all text to lowercase
options.D: It removes spaces from text

questions.explanation: PROPER capitalises the first letter of each word in a text string and converts other letters to lowercase, subject to its word-boundary rules.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the TODAY function do in Excel?

options.A: It returns the current date according to the computer or calculation environment's date settings and updates when the worksheet recalculates
options.B: It returns the current date and time
options.C: It creates a date value from supplied year, month and day numbers
options.D: It extracts the year number from a date value

questions.explanation: TODAY returns the current date according to the computer or calculation environment's date settings and updates when the worksheet recalculates.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the NOW function do in Excel?

options.A: It returns the current date and time according to the computer or calculation environment's clock and updates when the worksheet recalculates
options.B: It returns only the current date
options.C: It creates a date value from supplied year, month and day numbers
options.D: It extracts the month number from a date value

questions.explanation: NOW returns the current date and time according to the computer or calculation environment's clock and updates when the worksheet recalculates.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the DATE function do in Excel?

options.A: It creates a date value from supplied year, month and day numbers
options.B: It returns the current date
options.C: It returns the current date and time
options.D: It extracts the year number from a date value

questions.explanation: DATE creates a date value from supplied year, month and day numbers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the YEAR function do in Excel?

options.A: It extracts the year number from a valid Excel date value
options.B: It extracts the month number from a date value
options.C: It extracts the day of the month from a date value
options.D: It creates a date value from supplied numbers

questions.explanation: YEAR extracts the year number from a valid Excel date value.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the MONTH function do in Excel?

options.A: It extracts the month number, from 1 to 12, from a valid Excel date value
options.B: It extracts the year number from a date value
options.C: It extracts the day of the month from a date value
options.D: It creates a date value from supplied numbers

questions.explanation: MONTH extracts the month number, from 1 to 12, from a valid Excel date value.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the DAY function do in Excel?

options.A: It extracts the day of the month, from 1 to 31, from a valid Excel date value
options.B: It extracts the year number from a date value
options.C: It extracts the month number from a date value
options.D: It creates a date value from supplied numbers

questions.explanation: DAY extracts the day of the month, from 1 to 31, from a valid Excel date value.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the ROUNDUP function do in Excel?

options.A: It rounds a number away from zero, to the specified number of digits
options.B: It rounds a number toward zero, to the specified number of digits
options.C: It rounds a number to the nearest specified number of digits
options.D: It returns the absolute value of a number

questions.explanation: ROUNDUP rounds a number away from zero, to the specified number of digits.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the ROUNDDOWN function do in Excel?

options.A: It rounds a number toward zero, to the specified number of digits
options.B: It rounds a number away from zero, to the specified number of digits
options.C: It rounds a number to the nearest specified number of digits
options.D: It returns the absolute value of a number

questions.explanation: ROUNDDOWN rounds a number toward zero, to the specified number of digits.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the ABS function do in Excel?

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
